From 0fd2b00b2d3d05e3eaa13342b3dfb0fa85c226ae Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Adrian Korwel <adriank20047@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 09:58:32 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] USB: serial: io_ti: fix heap overflow in build_i2c_fw_hdr()

build_i2c_fw_hdr() allocates a fixed-size buffer of
(16*1024 - 512) + sizeof(struct ti_i2c_firmware_rec) bytes, then
copies le16_to_cpu(img_header->Length) bytes into it without
validating that Length fits within the available space after the
firmware record header.

img_header->Length is a __le16 from the firmware file and can be
up to 65535. check_fw_sanity() validates the total firmware size
but not img_header->Length specifically.

Fix by rejecting images where img_header->Length exceeds the
available destination space.

Fixes: 1da177e4c3f4 ("Linux-2.6.12-rc2")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Adrian Korwel <adriank20047@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/usb/serial/io_ti.c b/drivers/usb/serial/io_ti.c
index 6e0d4c38911b..d48819d785ef 100644
--- a/drivers/usb/serial/io_ti.c
+++ b/drivers/usb/serial/io_ti.c
@@ -844,6 +844,11 @@ static int build_i2c_fw_hdr(u8 *header, const struct firmware *fw)
 	/* Pointer to fw_down memory image */
 	img_header = (struct ti_i2c_image_header *)&fw->data[4];
 
+	if (le16_to_cpu(img_header->Length) >
+			buffer_size - sizeof(struct ti_i2c_firmware_rec)) {
+		kfree(buffer);
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
 	memcpy(buffer + sizeof(struct ti_i2c_firmware_rec),
 		&fw->data[4 + sizeof(struct ti_i2c_image_header)],
 		le16_to_cpu(img_header->Length));
-- 
2.34.1

## Modifications in Each File

### `drivers/usb/serial/io_ti.c`
- Added a bounds check in the `build_i2c_fw_hdr()` function.
- Before the `memcpy` that copies firmware image data into a fixed-size heap buffer, the patch checks:
  ```c
  if (le16_to_cpu(img_header->Length) >
          buffer_size - sizeof(struct ti_i2c_firmware_rec)) {
      kfree(buffer);
      return -EINVAL;
  }
  ```
- This validates that the `Length` field from the firmware header does not exceed the remaining space in the allocated buffer after the firmware record header. If it does, the function frees the buffer and returns an error, preventing a heap overflow.

## Relationship Between Modifications
The patch consists of a single change in one file. The modification directly addresses the vulnerability by ensuring that the unchecked `img_header->Length` value (which can be up to 65535) is verified against the actual available destination buffer size (`buffer_size - sizeof(struct ti_i2c_firmware_rec)`). This prevents copying more data than allocated, avoiding heap overflow. The check is placed just before the vulnerable `memcpy`, making it a complete fix for the bug.
